ca_sad_boulders.blurb: Sad Boulders is a bouldering area on the Volcanic Tableland about seven miles north of Bishop, California, where the floor of the Owens Valley steps up to a plateau roughly 300 feet high. The problems sit in canyons and washes cut into its southern rim, on Bishop Tuff left by a huge eruption of the Long Valley Caldera. Every climb here is a boulder problem. The grades run from V0 to V12, with a broad base of easy and moderate lines through V4, a solid middle in the V5 to V8 range and a thin tail of harder ones. Larger groups include Ice Caves, Prozac Nation Bluffs, Kindergarten Area and Sad Parrot Area, so a day can stay in one pocket or roam.

me_c_greater_portland.blurb: Greater Portland covers the climbing around Portland, Maine, and Casco Bay, spread from Freeport and the coast near Cape Elizabeth inland toward Sebago Lake. Almost all of it is bouldering, with only a few trad and top-rope lines. The biggest cluster by far is South Freeport Boulders, where the granite is sharp and the problems lean toward slabs and slopers, split into four sub-areas with short walks between clusters. Little Hill Boulders, Highway Boulders and Morgan Meadows add more. Grades center on V1 to V5, with a thinner top end past V8. There is no big cliff nearby, so the city works best as a base for small boulder outings or a stop on the way to bigger rock elsewhere in Maine.

qc_01_bas_saint_laurent.blurb: Bas-Saint-Laurent's climbing is centered on the Saint-André-de-Kamouraska cliffs in the Kamouraska area, which hold about half of the climbs and have routes for beginners through to advanced climbers. The walls at L'Amphithéâtre there are quartzite, with sport routes from the upper 5.9s to 5.12, and the cliffs can be busy on weekends. Across the region sport climbing dominates, with a spread of top-rope routes, some boulders and a bit of ice. Grades cluster from 5.8 to 5.12, with most around 5.10 and 5.11. Other places to explore include La montagne à Coton, Mont-Carmel, Montagne à Gamache and La Pocatière, so there is variety for a trip beyond the main cliffs.

qc_02_saguenay_lac_st_jean.blurb: Climbing in Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean is scattered around the Saguenay fjord and its surrounding towns. Sectors include Chicoutimi, Jonquière, La Baie, Sainte-Rose-du-Nord and Cap à l'Aigle, on the south shore of Lac Kénogami. The region's showpiece is Cap Trinité, a wall of roughly 300 metres rising from the fjord, made mainly of granitic gneiss. Trad and sport routes are about equally common, with a fair number of boulder problems and a little aid, ice and mixed. Roped grades mostly fall between 5.9 and 5.12, with a few harder lines. Bolted faces opened up steep blank walls here, and multi-pitch routes sit alongside the single-pitch crags.

va_haw_orchard.blurb: Haw Orchard is a bouldering sector of Grayson Highlands State Park in southwest Virginia, and every climb here is a boulder problem. Its largest cluster, Back of Beyond, sits at about 3,650 feet and is made up of many separate blocks, roofs and small boulder groups, so problems are spread out rather than concentrated on a few big stones. Wild Wood, Luminary Area and Deeper Downs hold more. Most problems fall between V1 and V5, with a good number of easy ones and a smaller set of hard lines up to V9. Parts of the area are still being developed. Climbers are a steady presence in the park from March through October.

ga_metro_atlanta_area.blurb: Metro-Atlanta climbing is small in scale and mostly bouldering, with some top-rope, a little trad and very little sport. Most of it lies along the Chattahoochee River and in boulder fields south of the city, among wooded pockets inside the urban sprawl. The Palisades is the largest single area, a quiet riverside spot of boulders and small outcrops. Island Ford and Morgan Falls each add a few dozen boulder problems, and Allenbrook has a short cliff used mainly for top-roping. Boulder grades center on V0 to V5, with a thin high end, while roped climbs run from about 5.6 to 5.11. Expect bold leads, easy top-rope setups and good bouldering rather than big walls.
